This site organises the **Agentic Software Development & Vibe Coding** series. It gathers the programme material and provides a roadmap of learning in the quickly evolving field of Agentic AI. The idea is to provide an overview and some guidance on how to develop our own skills to create and work with Agentic AI.

We are also creating a space for community contributions towards open-source and digital sovereignty. It gives students one place to find the lessons and the shared roadmap, and to track which classes are ready.

## Classes

### Session I: Introduction to the Vibe Paradigm

**Presenter:** Phyo Ko Ko

Key ideas of Vibe Coding. Setting up a standard dictionary of terms. What is Vibe Coding, and what are the best practices? How are people using Vibe Coding around the world?

Link for the presentation: [Presentation](materials/introduction_vibe_coding_phyo_ko_ko.pdf){.btn .btn-primary target="_blank"}

Link for the GitHub: [GitHub](https://github.com/phyo57/UNDP-Vibe-coding-Introduction-volunteering){.btn .btn-primary target="_blank"}

### Session II: Architecting and configuring the AI Workspace

**Presenter:** Ruiya Zhou

How can we properly configure the workspace for working with agents? Which software, tools and libraries are the most used? What do professionals in the field use? These and many more questions will be answered during the session.

Link to Drive: [Drive Folder of the Session](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1N5UJX2DxvKmK1E2eEwwWzkW4AotRNREJ){.btn .btn-primary target="_blank"}

### Session IV and V: Development paradigms: Intent-Based "Vibe" Iteration, Spec-Driven, Agentic Orchestration

**Presenter:** Akshi Rao

What is intent-based? spec-based or agentic orchestration? How does the meaning and the driving intents of your project matters for the outcome of LLMs? What are the human specifications for we need to set up when developing in the agentic AI era?

Link for the presentation: [Slides-Presentation](materials/Development_Paradigms_Vibe_Coding.pdf){.btn .btn-primary target="_blank"}

Link for the coding materials (this is a zip file to be downloaded): [Coding-materials-zip-file](materials/akshi-bhasker-rao-website.zip){.btn .btn-primary target="_blank"}


### Session VI and VII: Agentic Mechanics: Planning & Tool Use

**Presenter:** Alan al-jammar ·**Date: 14/11 5pm (GMT+3)**

What is the difference of a prompt and a agentic scheme? How can agents take their own decision? What are the ways to organize and plan the use of agents for a task driven approach? What are the most common ways to set up agents and config the environment? 
These and more answers in our class. You can watch the Theorical Session in our recordings. 

Forms given in Class: [Session 1 feedback: How AI agents think and act](https://docs.google.com/forms/d/11OjxCXNignMPoYWbO-q4OwjWOzmvJbCAkEXRaffv5w8/viewform?ts=6af86790&edit_requested=true){.btn .btn-primary target="_blank"}

### Session VIII and IX: Managing Multi-Agent Teams

**Presenter:** Lwin Ravendo, [GitHub](https://github.com/W4sP4nx2) **Status:** Ready **Roadmap session:** S5

Supervise an agent team through typed handoffs, scoped tools, independent checks and human decisions. The course starts with deterministic fixtures and ends with a Software Factory that builds a minimalist travel website using local files and Git operations. No LLM or API key is needed, so the cost is $0.00.

[GitHub](https://github.com/W4sP4nx2/Managing-Multi-Agent-Teams/tree/main){.btn .btn-primary target="_blank"}

[Slides](materials/s5-slides.html){.btn .btn-primary}
[Flashcards Study](materials/s5-flashcards.html){.btn .btn-primary}
[Reading List](){.btn .btn-primary target="_blank"}


### Session X & XI: Debugging in the Agentic Age

**Presenter:** Shakila Alam Aishy

Learn systematic debugging of AI-generated code. Session X covers four reasons AI code breaks and audit frameworks. Session XI is a live debugging lab fixing a real broken donation page, demonstrating security vulnerabilities and proper recovery techniques.

[Github Repository](https://github.com/shakila-alam-aishy/Debugging-in-the-Agentic-Age_UNDP){.btn .btn-primary}

[Session X Summary](Session_Summaries/Session-X_Debugging-in-Agentic-Cage.md){.btn .btn-outline-primary}

[Session XI Summary](Session_Summaries/Session-XI_Practical-Debugging-Lab.md){.btn .btn-outline-primary}

### Session XII: Context Engineering & Large Codebases

**Presenter:** Ekoko Clesh (Mozambique) · **Date:** November 25, 2026

Practical hands-on lab on making AI agents work effectively in real software projects. Learn to map repositories, write effective agent instructions, review AI-generated code safely, and use reusable project rules (agents.md). Includes real example of building a task manager web application.

[Session XII Summary](Session_Summaries/Session-XII_Context-Engineering-Large-Codebases.md){.btn .btn-primary target="_blank"}

### Class 9: AI-First SDLC: Deployment & Operations

**Presenter:** Seth Odhiambo, **Date:** December 01st and 2nd, 2026

How effectively softwares have been deployed and how the LLM can help software developers, builders and general public to make it robust for cybersecurity safety. Seth will show different operations used on daily basis that can help with students engaging on the topics of Agentic AI and Vibe Coding to proceed with the right path and tools.
